product.schneider-tower386sx70.summary: The 386SX System 70 variant, whose manual distinguishes its disk and controller assembly.
product.schneider-tower386sx70.history: The 386SX System 70 shared System 40's modular platform, with a distinct storage assembly in Schneider's 1990 manual. Its parts list adds a separate disk controller and cabling. The commercial name alone does not establish capacity: the manual says 60 MB, while MAME interprets the suffix as disk size. Both references are retained.
product.schneider-tower386sx70.warning: Historical sheet under research; firmware preserved, emulation unvalidated.
product.schneider-tower386sx70.technical: The sources disagree about the disk. Schneider's manual, p. 3, says 60 MB and lists controller 50502 and separate cables; MAME associates the System 70 name with 70 MB. Specimens and revisions still need comparison to resolve this without silently correcting either source.
Processor and memory form a removable card. The manual documents an 80386SX at 8/16 MHz, C&T CS8281 chipset and 80387SX socket; VGA I/O base board 50925 is distinct from CPU card 52482.

A BIOS is attributed to a System 70. The 64 KiB version 1.03 file is preserved and matches MAME's recorded SHA-1. That provenance does not guarantee compatibility with every revision or validated booting.
The manual and hashes of five family ROMs have been reviewed. BluMach 7968236c has no dedicated model; MAME marks tower386sx as not working. No POST tests have been performed.
Complete behaviour still needs validation. Board and ROM correspondence, storage variants, memory, keyboard, RTC, video, disks and ports must be checked in a dedicated implementation.

Memory upgrades follow specific combinations. Pages 41–43 specify 1, 2 or 5 MB using SIMMs; the keyboard controller is an 8742 and the RTC is in the 82C206. The 286 VGA AT's DS1287 is not carried over.

Video has firmware separate from the system. Two 32 KiB VGA 1.00 ROMs are preserved and checked against MAME; its notes describe ATI18800-1 and 256 KB. Correspondence with each physical revision and CEG upgrades remains unresolved.
Schneider, Service Manual 386 SX System 40/70, 60195, footer HD60250/4000/36/90: cover, p. 3 and pp. 41–43 reviewed; PDF preserved.
MAME, at.cpp, snapshot of 7 November 2026: BIOS 1.00a/1.03 provenance, VGA ROMs and non-working status; differs from the manual on System 70 disk capacity.
MAME 0.278 merged ROMs, Internet Archive: five files extracted from the previously preserved container, with SHA-1 and SHA-256 verified; unknown rights, local custody.
BluMach 7968236c: machine table preserved and inspected, with no dedicated Tower 386SX entry.
